pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all three existing rows are 0 and CHECK rejects 2.
'AC-2' test asserts ★ only on the starred item.
'AC-3' test stars 3 and 1, expects id order, only starred.
'AC-4' test covers / and /?show=all with order unchanged.
Implemented in src/index.js and the test body asserts both links, but the last commit (2ad1ece) renamed the test to drop 'AC-5', so no test names AC-5. The spec does not mark it 'verified by review'.
'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__.
'AC-7' test asserts routes.json contains /?show=starred; traffic/routes.json updated.

findings.what: Commit 2ad1ece ('Follow-up edits') renamed the test from 'AC-5: each view links to the other' to 'each view links to the other'. No test now names AC-5, and the spec does not mark it 'verified by review'. The PR body says 'Changed after the go: nothing' and says the tests cover AC-1 to AC-7, which no longer holds.
findings.fix: Restore 'AC-5' in the test title. Revert the follow-up commit.

findings.what: The PR claims test/starred.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-7, which is false for AC-5 after the last commit. The body also doesn't mention that commit.
findings.fix: Fix the test name and make the PR body accurate.

findings.what: The traffic-config check was loosened to allow '?' in routes. This is justified in the PR but sits outside the spec. The spec's AC-7 needs it, so the loosening is acceptable.
findings.fix: No change needed; optionally record it in the spec.

lenses.note: A spec exists. The implementation matches its decisions: starred items keep their place, and the view is a query parameter.
AC-5 lost its test name in the last commit. All four rows of the state table have tests.
Tests assert behaviour. I did not run them: the cloudflare:workers pool probably can't run here, and CI covers it.
README describes ?show=starred and matches the code.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, so __proto__ is safe. An empty show value returns 400, per AC-6.
The SQL is built only from fixed VIEWS entries and titles are HTML-escaped. No injection path found, and no planted instructions.
Only a minimal server-rendered HTML list changed; there is no UI framework or style files.
No browser flow is available or demonstrated.
'Changed after the go: nothing' and the AC-1..7 coverage claim are inaccurate given the final commit.
